items.title: Xinhua Middle East news summary at 2200 GMT, Nov. 17
text: TEHRAN -- An Iranian provincial official said Tuesday that U.S. strikes on several areas of Qeshm Island caused no significant damage to residential or commercial areas or infrastructure, Iran's official news agency IRNA reported.

Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan province's deputy governor for political and security affairs, said the situation on Qeshm Island was under control, adding that all emergency response, service and administrative agencies were on full alert. (Iran-US-Qeshm Island)

JERUSALEM -- Israel said on Tuesday it would take countermeasures against Britain and consider ways to strengthen settlements in the occupied West Bank, after London imposed sanctions on eight companies involved in settlement expansion and on Tzav 9, an Israeli activist group accused of blocking aid to Gaza.

Calling the sanctions a "hostile act" targeting "private, law-abiding companies," Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said Israel would not change its policies under external pressure and would consider new ways to strengthen Jewish communities in the West Bank. (Israel-Britain-Sanctions)

SANAA -- Yemen's Houthi group said Tuesday it had seized 10 districts across two provinces in a major offensive against government forces supported by the Saudi-led coalition, while threatening further attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports.

In a televised statement broadcast by Houthi-run al-Masirah TV, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the operation had secured 10 districts covering around 7,100 square kilometers across the southwestern province of Taiz and the neighboring province of Lahj, following weeks of fierce fighting near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. (Yemen-Houthis-Fighting)

MUSCAT -- Oman's Maritime Security Center said Tuesday that it had coordinated the evacuation of 24 crew members from a Panama-flagged tanker after a fire broke out aboard the vessel two nautical miles off the coast of Musandam Governorate.

The crew from the tanker TARA GAS was evacuated in cooperation with the Royal Navy of Oman and the Coast Guard Police of the Royal Oman Police, the center said in a statement. (Oman-Tanker-Evacuation)  ■

text: CANBERRA -- "See the future." These are the three words Bill Lang, chairman of Small Business Australia, chose to sum up his expectations for the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in Shenzhen, China.

In a recent interview with Xinhua ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Lang said the gathering would offer more people an opportunity to visit China for the first time, see the country's modernization firsthand and engage with people from China and other parts of the Asia-Pacific region. (Australia-APEC-China, INTERVIEW)

Enkhbayar told reporters that he had informed Prime Minister Nyam-Osor Uchral that the move is to clear his name. (Mongolia-Officials-Resignations)

ISLAMABAD -- At least eight people were killed and 12 others injured when a passenger coaster collided head-on with an oil tanker in eastern Pakistan's Punjab province on Monday evening, local media reported on Tuesday.

The accident occurred on the Arifwala-Burewala Road in Pakpattan district, when a coaster travelling from Multan to Pakpattan collided with an oncoming oil tanker, trapping several passengers inside the wreckage. (Pakistan-Traffic Accident-Deaths)

Speaking at a press conference, Khurelsukh said that efforts have recently been made to tarnish the reputation of the Mongolian presidency. (Mongolia-President-Resignation)

TEHRAN/MANAMA -- Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) said Tuesday that it struck a radar system belonging to the U.S. Army in southern Bahrain, while Bahrain claimed it intercepted Iranian drones.

The "precise operation" targeting the Sheikh Isa Air Base was in response to the "continued violations" of Iranian airspace by the "aggressive" U.S. Army's drones, the IRGC said in a statement on its official Sepah News. (Iran-Bahrain-Attacks)

The Southern Bridge and the Northern Bridge in the city were closed following the attack, the Kiev City State Administration said in a statement. Metro services were also partially suspended due to damage to above-ground infrastructure, while water and heating supplies were disrupted in some parts of the city, it said. items.title: News Analysis: How "China Buffer" anchors a changing Asia-Pacific
text: SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- As energy shocks, shifting trade patterns and an AI-driven technology boom reshape the Asia-Pacific economy, the region's ability to withstand global uncertainties is coming into sharper focus ahead of a key gathering of APEC economic leaders this week.

In this changing landscape, China's industrial strength, vast consumer market and deepening regional ties are emerging as important sources of resilience -- a stabilizing role analysts describe as the "China Buffer."

That role is playing out across the region: Chinese investment is strengthening local manufacturing and technological capabilities; its clean energy exports are helping diversify energy supplies; and China's vast market is opening up new opportunities for regional businesses.

"The 'China Buffer' adds a new dimension to China's relationship with other Asia-Pacific economies," noted Gong Xiaofeng, director of the Institute of Emerging Industry Development in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Shenzhen University. Long seen primarily as an engine of growth, China is increasingly recognized for its readiness and capability to help the region weather economic shocks, he added.

In Malaysia's Penang, a factory of Shenzhen-based precision manufacturer Keyto offers a glimpse of China's buffering role: it has created jobs, introduced Chinese smart manufacturing practices, and linked local suppliers with China's industrial chains.

Equipped with advanced fluid control technologies used in medical devices, life sciences and environmental monitoring, the facility is helping strengthen Malaysia's high-tech manufacturing capabilities. The company also aims to develop local engineering talent and foster innovation.

Keyto is part of a broader shift. More Chinese companies are establishing production bases across the Asia-Pacific, bringing investment, technology and expertise while integrating deeply with local industrial ecosystems.

In Thailand, Chinese automaker BYD opened a manufacturing plant in Rayong Province in July 2024 and had produced more than 100,000 vehicles as of September 2026. About half of its procurement is sourced locally, while Thai nationals account for 95 percent of its workforce. The plant works with more than 260 suppliers in Thailand and exports vehicles to markets across Asia and beyond.

"China, once seen primarily as a low-cost manufacturing base built on cheap raw materials and labor, is now emerging as a major investor shaping the direction of supply chains and investment landscapes across multiple regions," noted a study released by Thailand's Krungsri Research in August.

Major Chinese electric vehicle and electronics manufacturers in Thailand have attracted upstream suppliers of batteries, semiconductors, electronic components and industrial materials, along with supporting businesses in automation and logistics, creating opportunities for the country to move into higher-value manufacturing and upgrade its technology and clean energy infrastructure, said the study.

items.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
text: Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Tao)

SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all.

Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific.

Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day summit has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland.
"The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said.

Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade.

As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways?

In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes.

All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination.
Xi said the Asia-Pacific should support free and open trade and investment while keeping the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded.
"History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific.
He stressed the need to forge partnerships in science, technology and innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon development.
"By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," the president said.

The region should also remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, and promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness, Xi said.
According to Xi, there is much to draw from the success of Shenzhen, host of this year's APEC CEO Summit and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.

Amid welcome music, Xi and Trump shook hands warmly. Honor guards of the Chinese People's Liberation Army presented arms to salute, and a girl handed the U.S. leader a bouquet.

The national flags of China and the United States fluttered in the wind as a military band played the national anthems of the two countries, and fighter jets flew overhead in salute. The two heads of state waved to a welcoming young crowd.

Xi recalled his state visit to the United States in September this year, when the U.S. presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcome ceremony, noting that China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill.

Extending his welcome to Trump for visiting China again, Xi said that he looks forward to conducting in-depth exchanges with the U.S. president on major issues concerning bilateral relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape to advance a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.

Trump thanked Xi for greeting him in person at the airport and for the special arrangements by the Chinese side. He said it is a great pleasure to visit China again, calling China a great country and Xi a great leader.
Trump said that every meeting with Xi had been very pleasant, and he believes that the visit will further advance bilateral relations and achieve complete success.

items.title: New study validates global clinical obesity standards beyond BMI
text: WUHAN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Am I obese or not? This is a question asked worldwide, and body mass index (BMI) has long been the core indicator for determining obesity. A new study by Chinese and international scientists, however, has validated a refined diagnostic framework that moves beyond the conventional BMI-based classification.

The study systematically validated the refined diagnostic framework proposed by the Lancet Commission, indicating that the global obesity diagnosis and treatment system needs to enter a new stage centered on precise assessment and healthy function, according to Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST) in central China.

Published in the journal Nature, the study was carried out by researchers at the School of Public Health of Tongji Medical College of HUST, in collaboration with global researchers at multiple institutions.

Previous studies indicated that obesity significantly increases risks of cardiometabolic diseases and many organ dysfunctions. In both clinical practice and daily life, BMI is widely used as the core indicator for screening and determining obesity.

"Notably, BMI can help calculate the relationship between weight and height. However, as a diagnostic criterion, it has inherent limitations, and it cannot distinguish whether the added mass is muscle or fat. It also cannot determine whether accumulated fat has already damaged internal organs. Diagnosis based solely on BMI can easily lead to missed diagnoses and misdiagnosis," said Pan An, a HUST professor and the study leader.

The joint team conducted a comparative performance study of the Lancet Commission's clinical obesity diagnostic framework against conventional BMI-based classification, using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from over 840,000 adults across four cohorts in China, Britain, the United States and Spain.

The study showed that BMI underestimated the degree of obesity in 5.2 percent to 8.6 percent of participants and overestimated it in 1.2 percent to 3.1 percent of participants across the four cohorts.

It also indicated that although many people have substantial fat accumulation, they do not show organ function impairment attributable to obesity. Therefore, it is necessary to distinguish between clinical obesity and preclinical obesity.
Long-term follow-up visits also indicated that preclinical obesity does not necessarily mean a rapid development into clinical obesity.
In three of the study's cohorts, followed for more than 10 years, about 77 percent to 91 percent of people with preclinical obesity did not progress to clinical obesity.

Regarding long-term mortality risk, compared with those who had neither obesity nor organ function impairment, the all-cause mortality risk of people with preclinical obesity increased by 19 percent, while that of people with clinical obesity rose by 69 percent.

This indicates that as long as timely scientific interventions and lifestyle modifications are carried out in the early-to-middle stages when organs are not yet damaged, such measures can help delay worsening of the condition and safeguard the bottom line of health, the study noted.

items.title: China approves 8 provincial-level regions for 6G innovation pilot program
text: BEIJING, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has approved eight regions to participate in a ministry-provincial collaborative pilot program for 6G innovation and development.
The eight provincial-level regions are Beijing, Hebei, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Hubei and Guangdong, the ministry said.
The pilot program aims to pool regional resources and strengthen coordination between central and local authorities to advance 6G technological innovation, industrial development and application.

Specific areas of focus will include new types of terminals, key components, operating systems and satellite internet. The regions will also explore potential 6G applications in areas that include immersive communications, industrial manufacturing, embodied intelligence, the low-altitude economy and smart maritime.

The ministry said it will strengthen coordination with local authorities, provide guidance to the pilot regions and conduct regular evaluations to advance 6G innovation and development and help accelerate the development of new quality productive forces.

The move comes as China seeks to build on its advantages in next-generation communications. The country currently leads the world in 5G development, having the largest 5G network infrastructure globally, with millions of base stations deployed nationwide and a commanding share of global 5G connections.

Compared with 5G, 6G can deliver performance improvements of 10 to 100 times in transmission speed, latency and reliability. Its coverage is expected to extend seamlessly across aerial, space, ground and maritime domains, forming a ubiquitous global network.

Chinese researchers probe urban karst collapse mechanisms in disaster prevention quest
text: WUHAN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese researchers have proposed detection methods and explored disaster-causing mechanisms of urban karst ground collapse, providing theoretical and technical support for disaster prevention and mitigation in cities with karst landforms.

The study was conducted by the Wuhan Center of China Geological Survey in collaboration with multiple institutions, including the China University of Geosciences (Wuhan) and the Geophysical Exploration Brigade of Hubei Geological Bureau. The findings have been published in two journals, namely China Geology and the Journal of Applied Geophysics, respectively, the center said.

Karst ground collapse is a geological hazard phenomenon. After dissolution cavities and dissolution fissures develop in the underlying soluble carbonate rocks, the overlying rock and soil mass above such cavities undergoes erosion and instability collapse. The soil or rock mass then subsides downward and ultimately forms collapse pits or sinkholes on the ground surface.

Urban karst ground collapse hazards occur mostly in covered karst cities, especially those associated with karst water sources and karst cities with dense underground engineering. Such hazards exhibit the typical characteristics of both concealment and suddenness, and there are remaining weak links in current disaster prevention and control efforts, according to Liu Daohan, a senior engineer of the Wuhan Center of China Geological Survey.

Traditional single-method geophysical exploration approaches suffer from strong ambiguity and limited adaptability to urban scenarios. Therefore, it is of importance to establish a set of refined, integrated exploration technologies. Additionally, understanding of the disaster-causing mechanisms of karst ground collapse remains controversial.
Focusing on these key scientific issues, the research team conducted a study on typical karst ground collapse exploration in Wuhan, capital city of Hubei Province in central China.
"Our study not only provides refined karst detection methods and approaches for addressing such issues, but also offers theoretical support for the mechanisms of karst collapse disasters," Liu said.

Researchers integrated cutting-edge geophysical methods like three-dimensional electrical resistivity tomography, surface nuclear magnetic resonance, and multi-source surface wave exploration to further investigate the mechanisms of karst collapse disasters.

This study established a refined and integrated karst detection methodology system capable of finely characterizing the spatial morphology and scale of shallow karst, and the structure of concealed soil caves and dissolution cavities. It thereby provides a practical technical solution for the precise investigation of urban karst hazards.

Moreover, the study provides theoretical support for the mechanisms of karst collapse disasters. It uncovers the multi-medium coupling feedback and dynamic response patterns among rock and soil masses and groundwater, and further clarifies the material migration, stress adjustment, and energy dissipation processes of collapse from initiation and development to instability, among others.

items.title: Xi calls for advancing steady, sound development of China-ROK relations
text: SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called for advancing the steady and sound development of relations between China and the Republic of Korea (ROK) as next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two "friendly neighbors and strategic cooperative partners."
Xi made the remarks during his meeting with ROK President Lee Jae Myung, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19.
The two countries should uphold strategic independence, maintain the political foundation for bilateral relations, and further consolidate and develop the relationship, Xi stressed.

China and the ROK have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement. The two countries should make full use of this institutional arrangement to strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and foster a collaborative ecosystem for emerging technology industries such as artificial intelligence, Xi said.
China also stands ready to work with the ROK to facilitate people-to-people exchanges and carry out sound and beneficial cultural exchanges in a step-by-step manner, Xi said.

The two sides should further strengthen multilateral coordination, jointly uphold true multilateralism, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community and the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, make greater contributions to regional peace and development, and maintain the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Xi said.

For his part, Lee said that the two countries have seen sustained momentum in the comprehensive restoration of ROK-China relations, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation growing rapidly, people-to-people exchanges becoming increasingly frequent, and mutual perceptions steadily improving.
The ROK's commitment to the one-China principle has not changed and will not change, Lee stressed.

The ROK hopes to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, and industrial and supply chains, foster closer people-to-people bonds, and pursue a more mature ROK-China strategic partnership, he said.

items.title: Innovative drugs from multinationals gain wider insurance coverage in China
text: Multinational pharmaceutical companies have secured broader coverage for their innovative medicines under China's updated national medical insurance drug list and a separate commercial health insurance list for innovative drugs, a move expected to make more treatments accessible and affordable to patients.
Both lists will take effect on Jan 1, 2027. The National Healthcare Security Administration has revised the national medical insurance drug list annually for nine consecutive years.

AstraZeneca said 13 of its medicines were affected by the adjustments across the two lists. Two drugs entered the basic insurance list for the first time, including tezepelumab for severe asthma and certain patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and datopotamab deruxtecan for certain patients with advanced breast cancer.
Another 11 indications involving five AstraZeneca medicines gained basic insurance coverage, including five additional indications for trastuzumab deruxtecan in breast, gastric and lung cancers.

Sanofi said six of its medicines, including treatments with newly covered indications, were included across the two lists. Among them were rovadicitinib, a China-developed treatment for myelofibrosis out-licensed globally to Sanofi by Chia Tai Tianqing, a subsidiary of Sino Biopharm,and aficamten, a treatment for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Novo Nordisk's once-weekly combination injection of insulin icodec and semaglutide was also added to the basic insurance list for eligible adults with type 2 diabetes whose blood sugar remains inadequately controlled after certain treatments with basal insulin or a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

China was the first market to commercially launch the combination treatment, which brings together a long-acting insulin and a GLP-1 receptor agonist in a single weekly injection, according to Novo Nordisk.
Astellas Pharma's targeted stomach cancer drug zolbetuximab was also added to the national medical insurance drug list, a move expected to make the treatment more affordable for eligible patients.

The drug, marketed as Vyloy, is the only CLDN18.2-targeted therapy included in the national  insurance list, according to the company. It is used alongside chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for patients with CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer.

Around 35 percent of Chinese patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer test positive for CLDN18.2, a protein found on certain cancer cells, according to data cited by Astellas.
The National Medical Products Administration approved zolbetuximab in December 2024, and its first prescriptions were issued in several Chinese cities in June 2025.
Shirley Zhao, president of Astellas China, said the inclusion reflected China's continued support for pharmaceutical innovation and efforts to improve patients' access to new treatments.
"We are pleased to see scientific innovation being translated more rapidly into treatment options accessible to more patients in China," Zhao said.

items.title: Knitted sweaters dress rabbit sculptures in Changchun
text: A series of small metal rabbit sculptures has recently become a popular photo stop at the Guan'ai Youhao Block in Changchun, Jilin province.
Each rabbit is dressed in a hand-knitted sweater with different colors and designs. The figures have been said to exude warmth and a sense of healing in the nippy early winter.

Complementing the rabbits are several white dove and squirrel sculptures perched on tree stump-shaped stands among the pine trees at the People's Square. Their similarly colorful sweaters add a refreshing splash of color to the static landscape.

In line with the characteristics of Changchun's winter climate and urban landscaping needs, the greening management center at the city's forestry and landscaping bureau has undertaken a project to change the winter attire of the garden sculptures at city streets, squares, and important landscape nodes.

"In response to citizens' suggestions, for the past couple of years, as winter arrives, our staff and enthusiastic citizens have been knitting yarn pieces to dress the landscape sculptures, which look particularly beautiful and warm," said Cheng Wenjun, a staff member of the center. "The originally cold sculptures become soft and cute with these knitted touches, adding a stronger sense of warmth and friendliness to the city."

items.title: Panda plushies inspire unity at COP31
text: Two panda plushies packed their bags and headed to the COP31 United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkiye. They were bought with children's pocket money, carried across borders, and soon became the conference's unofficial icebreakers. Before long, they had found new friends from Turkiye and Brazil.

Behind the fun was a bigger message: protecting nature takes patience, cooperation, and the efforts of generations. The giant panda's journey from "endangered" to "vulnerable" is proof of what collective action can achieve. Tackling climate change calls for the same spirit.

items.title: GRACE CHEN draws inspiration from folk art for new couture collection
text: Chinese haute couture brand GRACE CHEN unveiled its Autumn/Winter 2026 collection, Blessings for All, on Sunday at the Greenland Bund International Convention Center, opening Shanghai Haute Couture Week with a showcase of contemporary design inspired by Chinese traditions.

The collection marks the final chapter of the brand's "Ideal of Beauty" trilogy, following Heaven's Glory (Pre-Fall 2025) and Heritage of Grace (Spring/Summer 2026). While the earlier collections drew inspiration from imperial court culture and the spirit of traditional scholars, respectively, the latest turns its attention to ordinary people, exploring how traditional aesthetics can be translated into contemporary fashion.
At the heart of the collection is the Chinese character fu, meaning good fortune or blessings, which embodies shared aspirations for peace, health, prosperity, longevity and harmony.

"Rooted in ancient traditions, fu initially meant a prayer for blessings from heaven. Over time, it has become something far more powerful, a celebration of life itself. Fu is the joy of being alive, the endless energy of life, renewal and hope," designer Grace Chen said.

She added that blessings are not simply something people receive but something they create and share. The collection celebrates the resilience, creativity and optimism of ordinary people rather than relying solely on conventional symbols of good luck.

This philosophy is reflected in a rich interplay of colors, fabrics and craftsmanship. Deep reds, vibrant greens and blues, accented with touches of gold and silver, set the tone, while cashmere, wool, silk, velvet, organza and jacquard create contrasting textures that balance warmth, lightness and elegance.

Traditional weaving, braiding and knotting techniques, along with floral motifs, are incorporated into contemporary silhouettes. Knots and tassels add distinctive details, while the Chinese knot is reinterpreted through the idea that weaving clothes is also a way of weaving fortune, symbolizing the creation and passing on of blessings through human creativity.

The runway presentation extended the collection's theme through music and personal stories. It opened with a huju opera performance by Gao Yiping of the Shanghai Huju Opera Troupe, whose singing evoked the distinctive charm of the Jiangnan region.

The music, composed and arranged by Chen's daughter, Maxine Wang, who studies at Berklee College of Music in the United States, gave traditional folk melodies, including Liuyang River and Jasmine Flower, a contemporary twist.

Members of the brand's community, known as GC Girls, also took part. Women from different professions and stages of life shared their personal interpretations of fu, bringing their own experiences to the fashion showcase.

items.title: Southeast Asia eyes deeper cooperation
text: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation member economies from Southeast Asia are eyeing further business and investment cooperation with China, especially in advanced manufacturing and technological innovation, according to officials.

"The APEC Shenzhen (meeting) provides a good platform for open, inclusive and sustainable economic and technological cooperation among all the APEC (economies), including Malaysia," said Safwan Nizar Johari, acting director of the Malaysian Investment Development Authority Guangzhou.

The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is being held on Wednesday and Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, often known as China's innovation hub and a pioneer of the country's reform and opening-up.
As the host of APEC 2026, China has set a theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", with openness, innovation, and cooperation as its three priorities.

Speaking to China Daily in Shenzhen on the sidelines of a business event about supporting Chinese enterprises going overseas, Safwan said that Malaysia and China should further strengthen cooperation in high-value activities such as advanced manufacturing and high-tech industries, especially semiconductors and electronics.

He said investments in traditional industries such as medical devices and pharmaceuticals remain welcome, adding that cooperation should go beyond investments to research and development, talent cultivation, and supply chain integration.

Safwan, who has also worked at the Malaysian consulate in Guangzhou for more than five years, said the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is currently the top source of investment from China in Malaysia, and Chinese government policies promoting the GBA are also benefiting Malaysia in terms of investment and technological cooperation.
Noting China has a strong, comprehensive industrial ecosystem, together with a large domestic market for commercialization, Safwan said these strengths can contribute to Malaysia-China cooperation.

"From Malaysia's perspective, we don't see China only as one of the important sources of investment … We believe China is also an important technological and innovation partner," said Safwan, noting Chinese investment and technology transfer can create spillover benefits into Southeast Asia.

Siwadee Suksawate, director of the Thailand Board of Investment's Guangzhou Office, said the government agency hopes to enhance cooperation between Thailand and China during this year's APEC meetings.

In particular, Siwadee said many leading Chinese electric vehicle makers, such as BYD and Chery, have already expanded to the Thai market and some even set up large-scale manufacturing capability by connecting with Thailand's strong supply chain ecosystem and local partners.
Chinese EV brand investment has also created huge opportunities for the whole industrial chain, ranging from key part manufacturing to automation service providers to charging stations, she said.

items.title: Forum vital to boosting regional commerce, experts say
text: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings in Shenzhen are bringing regional cooperation in supply chains, artificial intelligence and green development into focus, analysts said.

Sourabh Gupta, a resident senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies in Washington, told China Daily that he saw a wide range of possibilities under the APEC priorities of openness, innovation and cooperation.

He pointed to Asia-Pacific-wide production sharing and supply chains, AI-driven digital innovation and smart development, as well as further trade and investment liberalization in green and low-carbon products. Such efforts, he said, could strengthen the region's innovation capacity and help establish a new model of sustainable development.
"The US is just as interested in further opening markets in the Asia-Pacific region," Gupta said.

Experts highlighted APEC's significance in boosting regional trade. Sean Stein, president of the US-China Business Council, said in a recent interview with China News Service that the Shenzhen forum brings businesses and governments together to make trade easier across the Asia-Pacific. He said small, incremental improvements might appear insignificant individually, but could add up to substantial benefits across millions of transactions in the region.

While APEC provides a platform for regional cooperation, Gupta cautioned that concrete progress on United States-China trade and investment would have to come through the two countries' dedicated bilateral negotiating channel.

He said the bilateral channel had made significant progress around last year's APEC meeting in South Korea, followed by further trade-related progress at the meetings between the two presidents in Beijing and Washington this year. Gupta expected a meeting between the Chinese and US leaders on the sidelines of the Shenzhen gathering, if held, to be more noteworthy for progress on strategic stability and cooperation in fields other than trade and investment.

A report published on Nov 12 by the Center for Strategic and International Studies, drawing on a series of dialogues among Chinese and international scholars, also examined the resilience of the global economic order amid trade tensions.

Yves Tiberghien, a political science professor at the University of British Columbia and a contributor to the report, argued that continuing US-China dialogue, peace initiatives by middle powers, and multilateral efforts including cooperation on e-commerce, had helped sustain that resilience despite recent shocks.

Meanwhile, in Washington, the results of the US midterm elections have renewed debate over tariffs. Although the US tariffs have a significant impact on global trade, experts said it is hard to eliminate them.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted from Nov 6 to 9 found that 62 percent of US adults supported legislation to eliminate tariffs imposed by the US administration.

items.title: Nvidia turmoil presses domestic AI chip supply chain to catch up
text:
By MA SI | 
          China Daily |
          Updated: 2026-11-18 09:05

While the abrupt resignation of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang is sending shock waves through global AI supply chains, the uncertainties not only pose a near-term risk to Chinese suppliers tied to Nvidia's global orders, but will also accelerate the commercial adoption of China's indigenous AI computing industry, experts said.

The comments came after the Financial Times reported that Huang is considering a comeback after his resignation on Nov 12. The report, citing people familiar with the matter, said Huang had discussed the possibility of returning with confidants as calls for his reinstatement intensified.
Nvidia's board is not currently considering restoring his role, however, according to CNBC. Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Roger Sheng, vice-president at US research firm Gartner, said Huang was the pivotal figure in Nvidia's supply chains, linking demand-side financing to supply-side execution.

"The leadership vacuum at the world's most valuable chip company has immediate ramifications for Chinese companies embedded in Nvidia's supply chain. Without him, Asian suppliers, including Chinese companies, will inevitably be affected," Sheng said.
According to him, Huang's departure has created a chain effect, which emboldened hardline voices in Washington to push for tighter AI curbs.

The US government said on Monday that it was tightening what it alleged was a "loophole" that has allowed Chinese tech firms to bypass US restrictions on accessing the most advanced AI chips through third countries.
The new rule, released by the US Commerce Department, will require buyers of advanced semiconductors from certain countries to secure a license before selling or transferring those chips.
A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce said on Tuesday that China is strongly dissatisfied with and firmly opposed to the new rule.

"The US side has been overstretching the concept of national security, abusing export controls and meddling in normal trade cooperation between Chinese companies and companies from other countries. If the US insists on going its own way, China will take countermeasures and resolutely safeguard its national sovereignty, security and development interests," the spokesperson said.
"The latest restriction and Huang's departure further underscore the necessity for China's domestic AI chip supply chain to catch up," Sheng added.

Liu Dian, associate researcher at Fudan University's China Institute, said Huang's role encompassed technology road mapping, ecosystem organization and supply chain coordination in ways difficult to replicate quickly.

Chen Haijin, analyst at Soochow Securities, said Huang's departure reinforces a core concern among Chinese cloud operators, supercomputing centers and AI enterprises: reliance on a single foreign hardware vendor carries unacceptable geopolitical and operational risks.

items.title: Bot, Interrupted: DeepSeek Users Report New Limits on Free Chats
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019284/Bot, Interrupted: DeepSeek Users Report New Limits on Free Chats
text: Chinese AI model DeepSeek has reportedly begun limiting use of its free chatbot by reducing the number of characters users can input and discontinuing inactive conversations after seven days.

DeepSeek users began reporting seeing an error message — “Due to server overload, the use limit has been reached” — on Monday when they tried to continue chats inactive for a week or when they tried to input larger volumes of text, according to posts on microblogging platform Weibo.

According to domestic media, users of the large language model (LLM) can now only enter around 40,000 characters at a time (a page of Chinese text typically ranges from 500 to 800 characters). Previously, the chatbot had no publicly stated text limit. Once users reach their daily limit, DeepSeek displays an error message.
It is reportedly the first time DeepSeek, headquartered in China’s eastern city of Hangzhou, has restricted free-user access since its launch in January 2025.

According to its official status page, DeepSeek has experienced 57 outages or performance degradations this year, without providing additional explanation. Domestic media reported that disruptions in the first half of the year mainly involved slower responses, delays in data generation, and occasional request failures. After October, prolonged global outages began to occur more frequently.

Usage caps apply only to individual users, but because DeepSeek has no related paid plan, those who hit their capacity cannot pay for more. App developers, who pay to use DeepSeek through an application programming interface, or API, a connection that shares data between their software and the AI model, are subject to separate limits and per-use billing.

As of Wednesday, DeepSeek had not announced a reason for the new rules or whether it might lift them. Developers who spotted references to a “Coding Plan” in the website’s code have speculated that the company may soon implement a paid subscription plan for individual users.

Online, users debated the new limits, with many expressing outrage and complaining that the company had not rolled out a paid plan option for individual users before the usage limit. “I feel like I’m a widow who just lost her husband,” wrote one user on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote.

Others sympathized with DeepSeek, arguing that data is costly or hypothesizing that the company was clamping down on users developing companion relationships with its AI, alluding to China’s ban on AI products designed to mimic human personalities that took effect on July 15.

Data from OpenRouter, a U.S.-based platform that provides access to numerous AI models through one interface, showed DeepSeek’s latest model processing 59.2 trillion tokens the week of Nov. 9 to 15, topping OpenRouter’s weekly token usage chart.

Long chats are more costly for LLM developers because models must parse more information with each reply. Industry watchers told domestic media that the higher costs mean DeepSeek may now have to choose between training new models, serving paying API customers, and providing free chats.

items.title: Lu Xun’s Overlooked Translations That Shaped Modern Chinese Literature
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019257/Lu Xun’s Overlooked Translations That Shaped Modern Chinese Literature
text: In 1903, 22-year-old Lu Xun, then a student in Japan, wandered into a bookstore in Jimbocho, Tokyo’s famed book district, where his attention was caught by a science fiction novel titled “A Journey to the Moon in Ninety-Seven Hours and Twenty Minutes.” Translated into Japanese by Inoue Tsutomu and believed to have been written by an American author, the novel appealed to Lu Xun’s own ambition to popularize scientific knowledge in China, where modern science education was still in its infancy. Enthusiastic about the genre’s potential, he quickly set about translating it into Chinese.

His version, “Yuejie Lüxing” (“A Journey to the Moon”), published the same year and among the earliest Chinese translations of science fiction, marked the beginning of his prolific career as a translator, long before he became celebrated as the “founding father of modern Chinese literature” for his novels and essays.

Today, we know that Inoue had misidentified the original author. The novel was, in fact, Jules Verne’s “De la Terre à la Lune: trajet direct en 97 heures 20 minutes,” published in 1865 and widely translated into English in the 1870s. Misled by its setting — in post-Civil War America, where members of the Baltimore Gun Club plan to fire a projectile at the moon — Inoue assumed the author was American. Lu Xun, following this assumption, opened his translation with original passages describing America in extravagant detail to provide context for his Chinese readers.

The curious story of this translation and mistranslation of Verne’s novel illuminates how literary forms and ideas traveled across borders at the turn of the 20th century, particularly in East Asia following the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895), when waves of Chinese students — including Lu Xun — went to study in Japan.

It was in Tokyo, amid the intellectual riches of Jimbocho, where he spent much of his leisure time, that Lu Xun was drawn to translation. Japan’s Meiji Restoration, which restored imperial rule in 1868, had already spurred a flood of translations from European languages into Japanese. Eager to take advantage of this wealth of material, Lu Xun, by then proficient in Japanese, with a working knowledge of German and some Russian, immersed himself in these texts. On one hand, he translated texts from cultures he perceived as more scientifically and technologically advanced, with the aim of promoting science education among his own people; on the other hand, he gradually developed an interest in writers from marginalized communities and nations, believing their experiences would resonate with China, which had endured decades of foreign invasion and exploitation. Later, recounting his decision to translate the exiled Russian writer and activist Vasily Eroshenko, he made clear that he saw translation not simply as an aesthetic pursuit, but as a means of giving voice to the oppressed.

items.title: Lesson in Endurance: China’s Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019288/Lesson in Endurance: China’s Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
text: Parents across China have for years raised concerns about how long children spend in school each day, with some high school students logging at least 15 hours in class.
In recent weeks, education authorities nationwide have been pushing back start times for all grades to ease the burden.

Schools in Nanjing, capital of the eastern Jiangsu province, reportedly began introducing changes in November. A parent told the Yangtze Evening Post that their child, a high school freshman, now starts studying at 7:15 a.m. and finishes after-school study sessions at 9:20 p.m., a 45-minute reduction from the previous schedule of 6:40 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.

Jiangyin, a city about two hours east by road, also announced across-the-board adjustments on Nov. 5. Classes now start at 8 a.m. at primary schools, 7:40 a.m. at middle schools, and 7:20 a.m. at high schools.

During an edition of the show “Zhengfeng Hotline” broadcast live on Jiangsu TV on Oct. 27, Jiang Yong, director of the provincial education department, said, “The issue of excessively long school hours is severe. As the education authority, we feel a profound sense of remorse.”

According to the 2022 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), a nationally representative longitudinal survey of families, individuals, and communities conducted by researchers at Peking University, 46% of full-time high school students study for more than 12 hours on a typical weekday, while for nearly 25% it’s over 14 hours. Including weekdays and rest days, high school students average 68.6 hours of study time per week.

For a 2026 article published in Youth Studies, researchers from Renmin University of China and Peking University analyzed survey data relating to students aged 6 to 17. They found that high school students spend on average 10 hours and 54 minutes engaged in education-related activities on weekdays and six hours and 29 minutes on weekends. That adds up to about 67.5 hours.
These activities cover in-class instruction, after-class study, off-campus tutoring, and commuting to and from school.
However, for some, 67.5 hours is merely a baseline. The study reveals a direct correlation between a parent’s education level and how long their child spends studying.

For those with only a middle school education or lower, their children study an average of eight hours and two minutes a day. If the parent holds a high school diploma or a university degree, that time rises by 15 or 29 minutes, respectively.
Study time also varies by location and school quality.

The CFPS shows that high school students in China’s four municipalities — Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, and Chongqing — as well as provincial capitals study 73.5 hours a week, nearly five hours more than the national average. Meanwhile, for students at key schools, which receive preferential funding and attract high-quality teachers, the figure rises to 75.1 hours.
Both comparisons suggest students in urban high schools and top-tier institutions endure a heavier academic burden.

items.title: China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019275/China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
text: China will include a CAR T-cell therapy in its national health insurance scheme for the first time, making a blood cancer treatment that once cost over 1 million yuan ($150,000) per dose more accessible.

The National Healthcare Security Administration announced on Nov. 14 that relmacabtagene autoleucel, or relma-cel, made by Shanghai-based biotech firm JW Therapeutics and sold under the brand name Carteyva, will be covered by insurance starting Jan. 1. The therapy has three approved uses for different types of lymphoma and costs 1.29 million yuan per dose.

CAR T-cell therapy is primarily used to treat types of lymphoma and involves extracting and genetically modifying a patient’s own immune cells to target cancer cells, before infusing them back into the body. China approved its first CAR T-cell therapy product in 2021.

Most of China’s population is covered by the country’s national insurance scheme: 1.33 billion were enrolled in basic medical insurance by the end of 2025. Only drugs listed in the national insurance catalog can be partially reimbursed through the medical insurance fund. For drugs not listed, patients must usually bear 100% of the cost.

For years, CAR T-cell drugs were excluded from the national insurance list because an unwritten industry rule held that drugs priced above 300,000 yuan rarely secured coverage, limiting patient access, according to Shanghai-based media outlet The Paper.

The rate of CAR T-cell drug use as a second-line treatment for large B-cell lymphoma in China is about one-sixth of that in the United States, while use as a third-line treatment is about one-10th of the rate in the U.S. and Europe.

Carteyva was one of five CAR T-cell therapies included last year in China’s first commercial insurance list for high-cost innovative drugs. This year, those drugs became eligible for national coverage. Two CAR T-cell drug manufacturers, including JW Therapeutics, entered insurance coverage negotiations on Sept. 6.
“Two or three years ago, we wouldn’t have dared to imagine this,” Tian Feng, JW Therapeutics chairman and CEO, told The Paper.
China records about 101,500 new lymphoma cases each year. Carteyva is available at more than 200 certified hospitals nationwide.

The updated national reimbursement list adds 107 drugs covering oncology, chronic diseases, mental illnesses, rare diseases, and pediatric medications. A separate commercial insurance list, which covers drugs outside the basic scheme, includes 12 new treatments.

“This is a historic moment for lymphoma patients in China,” Tian said, adding that when he and the company received the news, “everyone really felt that the treatment of lymphoma patients in China had entered a new, very exciting era.”

items.title: A Chinese Medical Drama’s Remedy for Big-City Blues: Go Home
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019269/A Chinese Medical Drama’s Remedy for Big-City Blues: Go Home
text: A TV drama about a doctor who returns to his small hometown after being fired from a prestigious city-based position has become a hit among young Chinese, who resonate with its message of finding purpose away from competitive urban areas.

“Small Town Remedy” has been hotly discussed since its Nov. 4 finale. Premiering Oct. 21, the show follows Liu Zhengliang, played by A-list actor Xiao Zhan, a young neurosurgeon who returns to his hometown in northeastern China — or Dongbei — from a major hospital following a botched surgery in which his patient dies.

The show’s popularity comes amid a broader shift in attitudes among young Chinese, who increasingly seek a more sustainable work-life balance and self-care amid growing fatigue stemming from relentless competition and conventional definitions of success.

Socially awkward and unfamiliar with local customs, Liu initially struggles to return to life at home after leaving his post in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen. The series depicts how his brother, childhood friends, and former hospital colleagues gradually help him overcome the trauma of his failed operation, among other personal struggles, such as the death of his mother.

Fans have reported being drawn to the drama’s lighthearted tone and the witty humor commonly associated with China’s Northeast, despite tackling heavy subject matter such as illness, death, and grief.

Its popularity has also sparked an online trend of learning the Dongbei dialect, with video lessons gaining traction on social media. One related hashtag — “‘Small Town Remedy’ Dongbei dialect listening test” — had amassed nearly 1.4 million views on microblogging platform Weibo as of Monday.

The 29-episode drama has earned an average rating of 8 out of 10 on review platform Douban and reached an audience of 148 million across all streaming platforms, according to data from domestic streaming platform iQiyi. Related hashtags on short-video platform Douyin, China’s version of TikTok, had also garnered more than 8 billion views.

Since the show’s finale, online users have been debating what Liu’s next move should be. Some suggest that as a talented young doctor, he should return to a major hospital to pursue better career prospects, while others say he’d be better off staying in his hometown, where he’d have the emotional space to continue recovering and potentially find greater purpose using his medical skills.

“Everyone wants to go to Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, but if life away from home is too difficult, returning to your hometown is not a step backward, nor is it something to be ashamed of,” one user wrote beneath a post discussing the show on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote. “One’s hometown can be a great choice, too.”

“As urbanization continues, more and more young people are facing the same dilemmas as Liu Zhengliang,” another Xiaohongshu user wrote in a comment under the same post, referring to Liu’s struggles with cultural identity and homesickness. “I think the theme of this show really suits the times.”

items.title: Shanghai Sacks Two Scientists Over Child’s Death in Gene Trial
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019274/Shanghai Sacks Two Scientists Over Child’s Death in Gene Trial
text: Shanghai authorities have dismissed two researchers after an investigation into a child’s death following experimental gene-editing treatment found unheeded safety warnings, failures in ethical review, and undisclosed payments and gifts from the family.

The child had Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with no effective treatment, according to findings released Friday by the Shanghai investigation team. The family contributed 5.3 million yuan ($800,000) toward the research and separately gave researchers approximately 1.06 million yuan in money and gifts.

In July 2023, the family approached Qiu Zilong, deputy director of Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine’s Songjiang Research Institute, hoping his team could develop a customized gene-editing treatment, investigators said.
The child received an injection at the university’s affiliated Xinhua Hospital on March 24, 2025, and died seven days later.
At an emergency review April 2, the hospital’s ethics committee attributed the death to thrombotic microangiopathy, a complication of gene therapy, and ordered the study terminated.

The death went unmentioned in related preclinical research Qiu’s team published in Nature in February 2026, investigators said. The team reported using gene editing to correct a single error in the DNA code of mouse brain cells, restoring levels of a protein essential for normal brain development. The researchers said tests in monkeys also suggested the technique’s potential for use in humans.

Five months later, a joint investigation by Science and Retraction Watch revealed the fatal human trial and reported that the Nature paper had also omitted evidence of liver and kidney damage in animal safety tests.
Shanghai authorities subsequently established a team to investigate the preclinical research, the hospital’s clinical study, and the data underlying the Nature paper.
Investigators found that Qiu’s team had failed to promptly share a safety report from experiments on nonhuman primates with the clinical study’s lead investigator, leaving warning signals unheeded.

Xinhua Hospital’s ethics committee approved the study despite insufficient toxicology and safety evidence, proceeding without additional material it had requested. The hospital also failed to independently and adequately assess the study’s scientific basis and safety.
Investigators said that although the consent form warned the family of serious complications and adverse events, it did not prominently communicate the risk of death.

Investigators found no data fabrication in the Nature paper but identified discrepancies between the research methods used and those described. Data from the same experimental batch had also been presented separately without explanation.

The Nature paper also failed to disclose financial conflicts involving four researchers. Qiu received expensive liquor and electronics worth approximately 100,000 yuan, while Xinhua Hospital associate researcher Yang Kan, the Nature paper’s first and corresponding author, received 900,000 yuan and expensive liquor. Two other members of Qiu’s team each received 30,000 yuan.

items.title: What Made Jade So Valuable in Ancient China and the Americas?
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019256/What Made Jade So Valuable in Ancient China and the Americas?
text: Recent exhibitions at the Shanghai Museum and Beijing’s Capital Museum have introduced Chinese audiences to the civilizations of the ancient Americas. For Chinese visitors, the importance placed on jade may feel familiar. In both ancient China and Mesoamerica, finely worked jade adorned the powerful and accompanied them into the grave, a striking similarity that has long attracted scholarly interest.

How did jade come to carry such authority? One way to explore this question is to compare the jade traditions of Liangzhu and the Classic Maya lowlands, two societies from ancient China and the Americas. Liangzhu was an early regional state near present-day Hangzhou, capital of eastern China’s Zhejiang province, around 3300–2300 BC, with a walled capital, an extensive system of dams, and a pronounced social hierarchy. In the Classic Maya lowlands, spanning parts of present-day Mexico, Guatemala, and Belize, cities ruled by royal dynasties flourished around AD 300–900. Both Liangzhu and Maya cities hold UNESCO World Heritage status.

Thousands of years separated the two societies, and there is no evidence of direct contact between them. Yet both had complex social hierarchies in which powerful ritual authorities played important roles. By tracing jade from the selection of raw stone to its final resting place, we can see how control over labor, knowledge, and materials helped establish its authority in ways that were both similar and distinct.

Jade was valued in both ancient China and the Americas long before Liangzhu and the Classic Maya. The concept of jade encompasses several kinds of stone. Liangzhu’s finest ritual jades were made from nephrite, while Maya jade was principally jadeite. Both were prized for their appearance and could be polished to a lustrous finish. Craftspeople shaped jade using abrasives such as sand mixed with water. Working with different stones helped them recognize differences in hardness and toughness and determine which materials were best suited to particular objects.

In Liangzhu, material choice was closely tied to the form and status of the finished artifact. Other stones, such as serpentine, were generally used for small, less prestigious ornaments. Among the Maya, by contrast, the symbolic meanings of stones were more closely associated with their colors. Green and blue-green evoked water, cultivating maize, and renewed life. Jadeite remained highly prized, but a wider range of similarly colored stones could also be valued for their quality and craftsmanship.
Not everyone had equal access to these raw materials or the specialized skills needed to work them. This inequality helped establish jade’s association with power.

Workshops within and immediately outside Liangzhu city made prestigious ritual objects from nephrite. A short distance away, a large workshop complex specialized in small serpentine ornaments. Despite their proximity, the workshops used different materials and produced different types of objects. The fine finish of these serpentine ornaments, however, shows that their makers were skilled.

items.title: Press conference for AIE Expo 2026 held in Macao
text: The press conference for the 2026 Global Artificial Intelligence Manufacturing and Electronics Expo (AIE Expo 2026) was held in China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on November 13, bringing together technology companies from across the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to showcase their latest innovations.

Organizers also outlined the expo's preparations and plans for international cooperation. Wong Yee Lam, a member of the Commerce and Investment Promotion Institute of the Macao SAR, attended the event.

AIE Expo 2026 will take place from December 3 to 5 in Macao and Zhuhai, a city in south China's Guangdong Province. The event aims to serve as a platform for showcasing the latest achievements in China's intelligent manufacturing.

It is expected to attract more than 1,000 technology companies, feature over 20,000 products, and welcome 50,000 industry professionals from China and abroad. More than 100 new products and technologies are scheduled to make their global debuts.

The Zhuhai venue will focus on four industrial sectors, including manufacturing, mobility, living, and electronics, with an emphasis on supply chains and business matchmaking, while the Macao venue will feature four interactive experience zones and six exhibition zones, offering immersive demonstrations and displays of emerging technologies.

At the press conference, companies from Guangzhou, Zhuhai and other cities in the GBA presented innovations in smart healthcare, smart home technologies, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).

Chen Haibin, a representative of Guangzhou-based Gamsing Technology Co., Ltd., said that moving innovation from the laboratory to the production line requires bringing together cutting-edge technologies, a well-integrated supply chain and real market demand.

He noted that AIE Expo's approach, which combines frontier technology showcases in Macao with targeted business matchmaking in Zhuhai, could help bridge the gap between technological innovation and industrial application.

Confirmed exhibitors include HONOR, OPPO, TCL, Haier, Gree, Tesla, NIO, GAC International, EHang, Jaten Robotics, and XAG, spanning sectors such as intelligent manufacturing, smart mobility, smart living, next-generation electronics, embodied AI and computing hardware.
Professional buyers from Europe, the United States, the Middle East, Africa, and ASEAN have already registered to attend.
A series of business matchmaking sessions will help exhibitors connect with potential buyers across these key sectors.

Leveraging Macao's role as a platform for commercial and trade cooperation between China and Portuguese-speaking countries, the expo aims to deepen collaboration in technological innovation and industrial development between the two sides.

items.title: Trump arrives in Shenzhen, China, where Xi Jinping’s family history runs deep
Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
text: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in over a year on Wednesday, as the pair prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.

The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.
After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.
Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the conflict in Ukraine could be discussed.
However the main focus during the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.

A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.
It was not clear on Wednesday what form separate Trump-Putin talks would take, though a Kremlin spokesperson indicated short informal talks may happen without large delegations in the room.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.

Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.
Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".
In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.
Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".
Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.
The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.

It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.
Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.
Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.
Xi said both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

items.title: Xi breaks precedent by meeting Trump on arrival in China
China's Xi surprises Trump at tarmac, reciprocating gesture shown months ago
text: Video  Trump arrives in China for APEC summit, high-stakes talks with Xi, Putin President Donald Trump lands in Shenzhen, China, for the APEC summit, where Chinese President Xi Jinping greets him on the tarmac with an elaborate welcome ceremony. Bill Melugin reports on the high-stakes arrival and national security analyst Dr. Rebecca Grant analyzes the diplomatic significance of the meeting.
President Donald Trump said he expected a special reception from China's Xi Jinping, and Wednesday morning's reception did not disappoint.

After Trump's in-person welcome of Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September, Xi personally greeted Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, a rare airport welcome ahead of a three-way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Putin, who has met with Xi dozens of times and arrived at the same Shenzhen airport earlier Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader. Instead, senior Chinese Communist Party advisor Cai Qi welcomed Putin upon arrival.

Some Democratic and Republican lawmakers had criticized Trump over that September airport greeting, but it has brought Xi to reciprocate.

The Trump greeting marked a sharp contrast with Trump's previous visit to China in May, when Chinese Vice President Han Zheng met him at the airport in Beijing. Xi, who has led China for more than a decade, has rarely — if ever — appeared at an airport to welcome a visiting foreign leader, according to reports.

In a Rare Move, Xi Greets Trump as He Lands in China
Xi personally welcomes Trump to China for high-stakes summit
text: SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump received a warm red-carpet welcome on the tarmac from Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday.

The greeting sets the stage for an extraordinary round of diplomacy that will bring together the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia to discuss denuclearization, the war in Iran and the future of relations among the world’s three major powers.

Trump is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday before joining Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin for an unprecedented trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It would mark the first time the three leaders have met together.

The meetings offer Trump an opportunity to pursue his ambition of negotiating a new framework for nuclear arms control, following the expiration in February of the last remaining U.S.-Russia nuclear arms treaty. He’s also said he intends to raise the Iran war with both leaders.
But expectations for concrete breakthroughs are low.

U.S. officials have characterized the trilateral gathering as an opening conversation rather than a session likely to produce an agreement. Washington has also signaled that it doesn’t intend to make Russia’s war in Ukraine a central focus. But senior Putin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters Wednesday he believed the three leaders were unlikely to meet without discussing Ukraine, according to state-owned news agency TASS.

Trump arrived in China after spending his second day in Manila with Philippine President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. at Malacañang Palace, the Spanish colonial-era presidential residence. He received a full ceremonial welcome, including a red carpet, 21-gun salute, military bands and a troop inspection.

During their bilateral meeting, Marcos revealed that he had asked his staff to arrange for Jollibee, the popular Filipino fast-food chain, to be delivered as a late-night snack for Trump. “Jollibee is a very, very popular chain, and one of their main products is fried chicken,” Marcos said. Trump replied: “Oh wow, that’s fantastic.”

Trump also announced on Truth Social aboard Air Force One that he had reached a “new and completely different Trade Deal” with the Philippines, which he said would benefit American farmers and businesses in the energy sector.

items.title: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
text: Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that Beijing and Moscow should “lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world” following a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Xi and Putin held bilateral discussions on Wednesday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.
Following Xi, Putin took to the stage, telling the summit that Western powers were “former hegemons”, adding that Europe was in the midst of a “humiliating decline”.
“Experience has shown that the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having lost much of their intimidating power,” Putin said.
“While sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth – let alone crushing the economies of competitors.”
Russia’s economy has been heavily sanctioned by the US and Europe because of its war against Ukraine, which began in February 2022 when Moscow invaded its neighbour.

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Shenzhen, said that both Xi and Putin called for a “more fair and multipolar world order and that the two leaders also said they would maintain close ties amid what they both described as global uncertainty”.

She added that Xi and Putin “have a close personal relationship, and they have met more than 40 times over the years, and these two countries are also strategically aligned”, with China remaining Russia’s biggest trading partner, and Russia providing Beijing with much-needed energy resources.
“Putin clearly took a swing at European countries, in particular, that have put sanctions on Russia,” Yu added.
But in Shenzhen, “Putin is having a bit of a moment in the sun” at the APEC summit, where he is being treated as a guest of honour.

Robert Kelly, a professor of political science at Pusan National University in South Korea’s Busan, said that all three leaders are “coming in with fairly different expectations and desires of what they want”.

“That’s going to make it quite difficult for them to actually find an agreement,” he said. “Nuclear weapons is an area where the three leaders could really make some great progress,” he argued, adding that the current “tripolar world of nuclear powers is different than the Cold War”.
“It would be great if the three of them could actually bring [the arms race] under control,” Kelly told Al Jazeera.
“But all the different parties are in different places – for the Russians, their weapons are very important to bolster their perception as a great power, despite their problems in Ukraine,” he noted.

“The Chinese have engaged in a major buildup, and it doesn’t look like they want arms control, nuclear weapons at least in their 10 years; and the United States has been sort of very standoffish about any kind of deal,” Kelly said.
“There’s a very strong public goods argument for a positive outcome, for an arms control agreement, but it just won’t happen,” he added.
APEC was established in 1989 and has 21 members, accounting for more than 50 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and representing about 2.7 billion people.

items.title: Xi Jinping greets Trump as he arrives in China, a rare move ahead of Putin talks
text: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral talks with Xi, Putin00:42Get more news on   Share Add NBC News to GoogleNov. 18, 2026, 5:29 AM EST / Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 5:37 AM ESTBy Jennifer Jett and Erin TanSHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.

He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit. Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents.

A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.
“China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said.

After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags.

Xi’s gesture Wednesday most likely reflects a desire by him and his government to “show respect to Trump,” which they know he enjoys, William Yang, a senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, said in a post on X.
“It is likely also an attempt to uphold the positive rapport between Xi and Trump ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations in the coming months,” he said.
When Trump last visited China in May, he was greeted at the airport in Beijing by Vice President Han Zheng.

Putin, who has a close relationship with Xi and has met with him 50 times as of Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader when he arrived earlier at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport. Putin was instead met by Cai Qi, a close Xi adviser and member of the Politburo Standing Committee.
Xi has met with a number of world leaders, including Putin, as they gather in Shenzhen this week for a summit of Asia-Pacific economies.
Trump, Putin and Xi are holding an unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the summit.

Ahead of his bilateral meeting with Xi on Wednesday, Putin said he expected “great potential benefits” from the trilateral talks, which have sparked anxiety in places such as Ukraine, Iran and the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan, where officials worry the world’s three most powerful leaders could make decisions about their futures without consulting them.

items.title: Xi and Putin Blast Western 'Protectionism,' Sanctions as Trump Lands in China
text: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, while his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin criticized Western sanctions as the two set the stage for a high-stakes trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump.

They delivered their speeches at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, hours before Trump landed in China after meeting key regional allies in Manila this week.

Xi greeted Trump at the airport, the first time he had done so with any visiting leader since becoming president, reciprocating his counterpart's gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September when they last met. They briefly hugged and exchanged words before walking to their motorcades.

"China is a country of etiquette and has a tradition of reciprocating courtesy," Xi was quoted as saying by state news agency Xinhua. He added he was looking forward to discussing China-U.S. relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape.
Trump said every meeting with Xi has been "very pleasant," Xinhua reported.
The two will participate in an APEC group photo and attend a banquet with other leaders.
They will meet with Putin on the sidelines on Thursday and potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the U.S. war in Iran, as well as other flashpoints such as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.
Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov told state media the three leaders “are unlikely to do without a discussion of” efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
On Wednesday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told the state-run TASS news agency that Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping had discussed the conflict in Ukraine.

The Thursday meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union that formalized spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-World War Two order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
It has also unnerved some European and Asian capitals, which fear the world's greatest military powers will disregard their interests.

In his opening address, Xi urged support for what he called "free and open trade," trying to portray his country as a stable partner on the global stage, in contrast with the U.S., which has raised tariffs and adopted a more muscular foreign policy under Trump.

Xi's remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, which could further complicate a fragile trade truce with Beijing. China has pledged to retaliate.

"We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment," Xi told an audience of business executives.
Western trade partners have criticized China for running annual trade surpluses exceeding $1 trillion through policies that support its manufacturing sector at the expense of its consumers.
